cards.front: Define drift velocity $v_d$ of charge carriers.
cards.back: Average velocity of charge carriers in the direction of an applied electric field, superimposed on random thermal velocities; typically ~10^{-4} m/s in metals.

cards.front: State the expression for drift velocity in terms of current $I$, carrier density $n$, cross-section $A$, and charge $e$.
Define mobility $\mu$ of charge carriers and give its SI unit.
cards.back: $\mu = v_d / E$; unit: m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹

cards.front: Derive the expression for drift velocity assuming steady-state force balance with relaxation time $\tau$.
cards.back: Net force after collisions: $eE = m v_d / \tau$. Thus $v_d = \frac{e \tau}{m} E$.

cards.front: Write the microscopic expression for conductivity $\sigma$ in terms of $n$, $e$, and $\mu$.

cards.back: From $v_d = \frac{e \tau}{m} E$ and $J = n e v_d$, obtain $\sigma = \frac{n e^2 \tau}{m}$.

cards.front: Explain intuitively why drift velocity remains constant (not accelerating) under steady E-field.
cards.back: Continuous collisions with lattice ions randomize momentum; average velocity reaches terminal value when electric force balances collision drag.

cards.front: How does conductivity depend on temperature in metals via mobility?
cards.back: Higher T increases lattice vibrations, shortens $\tau$, lowers $\mu$ and thus $\sigma$ (resistivity rises).
